 161 [VPN] ## VPN Security Zones
 163 [VPN] Route-based VPN tunnel interfaces may be assigned to security zones.
 165 [VPN] A dedicated VPN zone may be used.
 169 [VPN] vpn
 183 [VPN] VPN traffic may require security policies between:
 185 [VPN] - Internal zone and VPN zone
 186 [VPN] - VPN zone and internal zone
 187 [VPN] - VPN zone and DMZ
 188 [VPN] - VPN zone and other destination zones
 203 [VPN] Route-based VPN traffic requires correct routing.
 213 [VPN] A VPN may be established while application traffic still fails because routing is incorrect.
 217 [VPN] ## NAT and VPN
 219 [VPN] NAT can interfere with VPN traffic if not designed correctly.
 223 [NAT] - Source NAT exemption
 224 [NAT] - Destination NAT interaction
 229 [VPN] Do not assume VPN traffic should be NATed.
 237 [VPN] NAT traversal may be required when one or both VPN peers are behind NAT.
 247 [VPN] Traffic selectors define which traffic should be protected by IPsec.
 256 [VPN] Selector mismatch can prevent VPN negotiation or traffic forwarding.
 262 [VPN] Legacy VPN configurations may use proxy IDs.

 289 [VPN] Perfect Forward Secrecy may be used for IPsec key negotiation.
 291 [VPN] PFS configuration should match the remote peer.
 293 [VPN] A mismatch may prevent successful IPsec negotiation.
 297 [VPN] ## VPN Monitoring
 299 [VPN] VPN monitoring may include:
 301 [VPN] - IKE status
 302 [VPN] - IPsec status
 313 [VPN] ## Useful VPN Commands
